title: A level line shows in its layer row thumbnail
goal: In the layers list, a perfectly level (or upright) line gets a blank thumbnail, while a sloped line shows its stroke, so you cannot tell the row is a line. The thumbnail should show the stroke whatever the line's angle.
notes: Seen 2026-10-04 running Scripts/playtest/click-click-draws-a-line-walk.json --no-build: snapshot 3-called-off-leaves-nothing-sc.png (copied to queue/audits/2026-10-04-click-click-line-3-called-off-leaves-nothing-sc.png) shows rows Line and Line 2 (sloped) with a thin red stroke and Line 3 (drawn with Shift, level) with an empty grey thumbnail. Theory, not checked: the thumbnail scales the layer frame to fit, and a level line's frame is only a few points tall, so the stroke scales below a pixel.
acceptance: A horizontal line drawn with Shift shows a visible stroke in its layer row thumbnail, in light and dark
A vertical line does the same
Sloped lines and arrows look as they do today

log.note: Reproduced in a unit test: a level 304x4pt line rendered to an 80x1 thumbnail, fitted into the 38pt slot at about half a point. Fix: DocumentRenderer.thumbnail takes minimumAspect; the layer row asks for 0.25, so a flatter picture is centred on a clear band at a whole-pixel offset. Shelf and component previews unchanged. Verified with LayerThumbnailTests (5 new), click-click-draws-a-line-walk (ok) and new a-flat-line-keeps-its-thumbnail-walk (ok, dark + light captures). Full suite green, 11261 tests.
